Ukraine sank a Russian warship docked in Libya and disabled a cargo vessel off the North African country’s coast, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday, in Kyiv’s latest attack on Russian assets far from the front lines.
The warship — identified as the 344-foot navy corvette Merkury — was attacked with seven maritime drones, sinking the ship and destroying a combat helicopter on board, Zelensky said in a post to Telegram.
Dramatic footage Zelensky released showed Ukrainian sea drones speeding toward the ship –– one of the newest ships in Russia’s fleet — which erupted into a giant ball of flames in the dock in Benghazi in eastern Libya. Photos taken by satellite imagery company Vantor showed the vessel submerged following the attack.

Spain’s Supreme Court shelved a criminal case against Catalan separatist and former regional leader Carles Puigdemont on Monday, thus removing the last legal hurdle for him to return to Spain following nearly a decade of self-imposed exile.
Puigdemont fled to Belgium in October 2017 after holding an independence referendum that the judiciary deemed illegal. The failed vote triggered a deep crisis between Madrid and the northeastern region, which has a distinct language and culture, as well as a significant secessionist movement that peaked in support that year.

Israel’s military assault on Gaza has caused severe environmental contamination, with signs of toxic pollution found across the entire territory, according to a report published by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (CEOBS).
The report, published Monday, said the extensive use of explosive and incendiary weapons, airstrikes and fires has made the air, soil and water too dangerous to live in for decades to come.
The scale and intensity of Israel’s bombardment have affected around 78% of Gaza’s landmass, with more than 99% of the territory experiencing potential contamination, the report found.

The lights were out. A thunderstorm had cut the power. But 8-year-old Tamizh Amudhan had a chess match to play against one of the best players in the world.
By the flicker of a candle, he sat on the floor of his family home in southern India, his laptop balanced on a pillow and its battery draining fast.
Still, the boy played on, pulling off a stunning upset against German grandmaster Vincent Keymer, then ranked world No. 7.
It was the kind of opportunity Tamizh might never have had if his parents hadn’t made a life-changing decision two years earlier.
In 2024, they left behind the stability of life in their hometown and moved to Sivakasi, a small town in India’s Tamil Nadu state, the epicenter of the country’s chess boom. There, they have restructured their lives around one dream: that Tamizh becomes the greatest chess player in the world.
